about: Files provgrep shows as permissive while debian/copyright records another license, each read by hand. verdict: debian-stale (upstream relicensed since Debian recorded it), debian-coarse (the files carry their own notice, which DEP-5 does not list), provgrep-wrong.

entries.why: The tarball's LICENSE and pyproject.toml say MIT; upstream moved from AGPL-3.0 to MIT in 2026, and debian/copyright still says AGPL-3.
The tarball's LICENSE and pyproject.toml say Apache-2.0; upstream relicensed from GPL-3.0 on 2026-08-17, and debian/copyright still says GPL-3.
Each file's header is the BSD-3-Clause notice; DEP-5 gives LGPL-2.0+ to everything outside */examples/*.
The header is the MIT notice of the libvirt-go project the code comes from.
Vendored libraries, each with its own LICENSE beside it (Unlicense; BSD-2-Clause, ISC-style and public domain) and matching headers; DEP-5 gives LGPL-2.1+ to the whole tree.
The header is the BSD-3-Clause notice of the BSD sys/queue.h it was copied from.
